lesson.title: La Familia Dedo: A Finger-Family Song
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Last week Sol marched a paper doll in a color parade. Today Sol brings someone special — [[la familia]], the family! Hold up one hand and wiggle your five fingers. Sol is going to turn every finger into a person in a family.

Point to your thumb — that is [[el papá]], the dad. Your pointer finger is [[la mamá]], the mom. Your middle finger is [[el hermano]], the brother. Your ring finger is [[la hermana]], the sister. And your tiny pinky is [[el bebé]], the baby! Now say Sol's finger rhyme, touching each finger as it comes: 'Este dedo es el papá, este dedo es la mamá, este es el hermano, esta es la hermana, y el chiquito es el bebé.'

Wiggle your whole hand and say '¡Todos juntos son la familia!' — 'All together they are the family!' Say the rhyme again, once fast and once slow, touching each finger. Then close your hand into a fist for a big family hug.
You turned one hand into a whole familia — el papá, la mamá, el hermano, la hermana, and el bebé! Tomorrow, look at a photo of your own family and point to the people you love.

objectives: Name five family members in Spanish — el papá, la mamá, el hermano, la hermana, el bebé — by touching the matching finger
Say the finger rhyme and call the whole hand la familia
materialsNeeded: Optional: a family photo to look at while you sing
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather with Sol and hold up one open hand where your child can see it.
2. Touch each finger and give it a name, having your child echo: thumb — el papá, pointer — la mamá, middle — el hermano, ring — la hermana, pinky — el bebé.
3. Say the rhyme slowly, touching each finger on its word: 'Este dedo es el papá, este dedo es la mamá, este es el hermano, esta es la hermana, y el chiquito es el bebé.'
4. Say it again together, letting your child do the finger touches this time.
5. Wiggle the whole hand and say '¡Todos juntos son la familia!' — explain it means 'all together they are the family.'
6. Play with the speed — one whisper-slow round, one fast round — then make a fist for a 'family hug.'
7. Point to a finger at random and let your child name that family member without the rhyme.
8. Close by asking: 'Which finger is el bebé? Which finger is la mamá?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: teach just el papá, la mamá, and el bebé today, and add el hermano and la hermana once those three feel steady
Ready for more: your child says the rhyme solo while you only do the finger touches
If your family says 'mami' and 'papi' at home, tell your child those are the same people — 'la mamá' and 'el papá' are the full words this song uses, and both are right
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken song-and-gesture activity — success looks like your child touching the right finger for each family word and trying the rhyme aloud, not a written answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Opens week 7's Cultures: Practices to Perspectives target (WA-WL-2015.2.1) by giving the child the family words that this week's photo-sharing, story, and show-and-tell all depend on. Matches the scope-and-sequence's Day 1 design — a family finger-play song, 'La familia dedo,' naming each finger family member — taught the way this K-2 band's oral/aural-first design calls for: a sung, physical, echo-based introduction with zero reading required.
